b2-09.title: Coffee break at work
b2-09.story: At eleven, Anna's team at her part-time office job finally took a [[coffee break]]. Max, who had been up since six, ordered a large [[americano]] and swore it was only his second that morning. Anna was trying to cut down on caffeine, so she asked for a [[decaf]] with oat milk instead. Lisa, who has recently become obsessed with green drinks, chose a [[matcha]] latte. Ira couldn't resist a mango [[bubble tea]] from the new place downstairs. Sofia came back from the gym with a [[protein shake]] and announced that a [[juice bar]] had just opened right next to it. "Trust me," Max said, "the [[smoothie bar]] across the street is much better." They argued about it for so long that Anna's coffee went cold. In the end, Max felt guilty and bought her a fresh [[ice tea]] with lemon, and everyone went back to work laughing.

b2-10.title: Lunch at the café
b2-10.story: On Friday, Anna and her friends went to the little café near the university, which has a huge lunch menu. Max couldn't decide, so he ended up ordering a [[club sandwich]] with a side of fries. Lisa went for a hot ham and cheese [[panini]], and Ira asked for grilled chicken on [[ciabatta]]. Sofia had never tried [[pastrami]], so she ordered it on rye and immediately called it her new favorite. Anna wanted something lighter and chose a warm [[pita]] filled with [[falafel]] and salad. Halfway through the meal, the waiter brought a [[fish burger]] that nobody had ordered, and it turned out to be for the next table. Ira admitted that she usually brings a homemade [[bento]] to class, but today the menu was too tempting. Max, still hungry, finished with two spicy [[samosas|samosa]] and green chutney. When the bill came, he promised to bring his own lunch next week, though nobody believed him.

b2-11.title: Sunday pasta night
b2-11.story: Every Sunday, Anna's family has pasta night, and this week it was her turn to cook. She wanted to impress her grandparents, so she decided to make two dishes instead of one. First, she boiled a big pot of [[penne]] and tossed it with homemade basil [[pesto]]. Then she started a slow [[bolognese]], adding a pinch of [[oregano]] just as her grandmother had taught her. Little Taras begged for spaghetti [[carbonara]], but Anna pointed out that they had run out of eggs. Dad, who never follows a recipe, fried some spicy [[chorizo]] and stirred it into the sauce when no one was looking. Mama had bought a pack of potato [[gnocchi]] as a backup, just in case something went wrong. In the end, nothing did, and Grandpa added a spoonful of [[ricotta]] to his plate and declared it the best meal of the month.

b2-12.title: Dinner out with friends
b2-12.story: For Lisa's birthday, the friends booked a table at a cozy restaurant that mixes European and Asian dishes. Max ordered the beef [[filet]] and asked for it [[medium rare]], which made Ira pull a face. Ira herself went for a classic pork [[schnitzel]] with potato salad. Anna started with crispy [[spring rolls|spring roll]] and a little bowl of [[sweet chili]] sauce for dipping. Sofia chose chicken [[teriyaki]] with rice and said the [[marinade]] was so good that she wanted the recipe. The chef came out to say hello and shared another secret: his lentil soup gets its flavor from smoked [[paprika]] and a spoonful of ground [[coriander]]. Lisa wrote everything down on a napkin, promising to cook it all for her friends next month. Then the waiters brought out a cake with candles, and the whole restaurant sang to her.

b2-13.title: Sweets at the market
b2-13.story: On Saturday, Anna took Taras to the weekend market, promising him one treat if he behaved. The first stall sold hot [[churros]] with chocolate, and Taras's eyes lit up immediately. Next to it, a small Turkish bakery was selling sticky [[baklava]] with honey and pistachios. Anna bought a bag of salted [[cashews|cashew]] for herself, since she never goes anywhere without a snack. Further on, they found an Italian cart with a dozen flavors of [[gelato]] and a bright lemon [[sorbet]]. Taras, of course, wanted everything, and by noon he was chewing pink [[bubble gum]] that a kind seller had given him for free. On the way home, they stopped by their grandparents' house, where Grandma had just baked an apple [[strudel]]. "So much for one treat," Anna laughed, as Taras reached for a second slice.

b2-14.title: A foodie's trip
b2-14.story: Max's sister Sofia is a real [[foodie]], so when she planned a trip to Spain with Anna, food came first. Before leaving, she spent hours reading a popular [[food blog]] and making a list of places to try. On their first night in Barcelona, they shared small plates of [[tapas]] and watched the street musicians. The next day, they had a huge pan of seafood [[paella]] by the sea. Surprisingly, Sofia's list also included a tiny [[sushi bar]] run by a Japanese family. Anna added far too much [[wasabi]] to her roll and had to drink a whole glass of water. The owner kindly brought her a bowl of warm [[miso]] soup to calm her mouth. On the last morning, they ate a slice of spinach [[quiche]] at a French café near the hotel. Still, when they landed in Kyiv, the first thing they both wanted was Grandma's [[borscht]].

b2-15.title: Drinks at the beach bar
b2-15.story: On the last evening of their vacation, Anna's family walked down to a small bar right on the beach. Mama ordered a jug of [[sangria]] to share with Dad, who preferred a [[mojito]] with lots of ice. Anna and Taras asked for two alcohol-free [[piña coladas|piña colada]], which came with tiny paper umbrellas. Taras was fascinated by the bartender, who spun a silver [[shaker]] in the air before pouring each drink. For an older couple at the counter, she mixed something stronger, adding a splash of [[vermouth]] to their glasses. When Dad complimented the service, the young woman smiled and said she was actually the [[bar manager]] and simply loved making drinks herself. She also recommended a [[wine tour]] in the hills nearby, and Mama booked it for next summer on the spot. Meanwhile, Taras announced that he wanted to be a bartender when he grew up, as long as he could do the tricks.

b2-16.title: Lunch at the mall
b2-16.story: On Saturday, Anna's family drove to the big new mall outside the city to do their weekly shopping at the [[hypermarket]]. By noon, everyone was starving, but they couldn't agree on where to eat. Dad wanted to try the [[steakhouse]] on the top floor, but Mama said it was too expensive for a quick lunch. Taras begged to go to the [[burger bar]], while Anna suggested the [[salad bar]] near the entrance. In the end, Mama suggested the [[food court]], where everyone could choose something different. However, it was so crowded that they couldn't find a free table, and the [[sandwich bar]] there had a line of thirty people. Luckily, Anna remembered that a new [[food hall]] with local dishes had just opened on the second floor, and it was almost empty. On the way home, they realized they had forgotten the milk and had to stop at the [[minimarket]] on their corner.
